_comment: Hand-written, page-specific cemetery notes appended to the veterans paragraph. Locations and statuses are from the VA National Cemetery Administration listings (cem.va.gov) and VA's state, territorial and tribal cemetery grant list, checked 2026-10-25.
burial-costs-indiana: In practice, Marion is the only national cemetery in Indiana for a casket burial; the Crown Hill annex is in Indianapolis, New Albany is across the Ohio River from Louisville, and the state-run cemetery is in Madison.
burial-costs-wisconsin: Northwoods, in Harshaw, is the one Wisconsin national cemetery VA lists as open for new burials, since Wood National Cemetery in Milwaukee is closed; the state-run cemeteries are in King, Spooner and Union Grove.
burial-costs-michigan: Great Lakes National Cemetery is in Holly and Fort Custer is in Augusta, near Battle Creek; VA's grant list shows no state-run veterans cemetery in Michigan.
burial-costs-massachusetts: Massachusetts National Cemetery is in Bourne on Cape Cod, while the two state cemeteries sit at opposite ends of the state, in Agawam near Springfield and in Winchendon on the New Hampshire line.
burial-costs-nevada: VA's Elko National Cemetery is still under construction, so for now Nevada veterans are buried in the state's own cemeteries, in Fernley east of Reno and in Boulder City southeast of Las Vegas.
burial-costs-connecticut: VA runs no national cemetery in Connecticut, which leaves the Middletown state cemetery as the in-state choice for an eligible veteran.
burial-costs-utah: Southern Utah National Cemetery is in Cedar City, and the state-run Utah Veterans Cemetery and Memorial Park, in Bluffdale, is the closer option for families around Salt Lake City.
burial-costs-georgia: Georgia National Cemetery is in Canton, north of Atlanta, and the state's two veterans cemeteries are in Glennville and Milledgeville.
burial-costs-illinois: Five of Illinois's six national cemeteries take casket burials; Fort Sheridan, on the North Shore, accepts cremated remains only.
burial-costs-minnesota: Fort Snelling is Minnesota's only national cemetery, but the state has four veterans cemeteries of its own (near Duluth and in Little Falls, Preston and Redwood Falls) plus the Leech Lake Band's cemetery at Cass Lake.
burial-costs-new-jersey: Finn's Point, in Pennsville, now takes cremated remains only, so a casket burial for a New Jersey veteran usually means the state's Doyle cemetery in Wrightstown.
burial-costs-washington: Tahoma National Cemetery in Kent takes casket burials, Vancouver Barracks accepts cremated remains only, and the state-run cemetery is at Medical Lake, west of Spokane.
burial-costs-wyoming: Cheyenne National Cemetery is in the state's southeast corner, and the Oregon Trail State Veterans Cemetery is in Evansville, next to Casper.
burial-costs-pennsylvania: Pennsylvania's open national cemeteries are near Philadelphia (Washington Crossing, in Newtown), Harrisburg (Indiantown Gap, in Annville) and Pittsburgh (the Alleghenies, in Bridgeville).
burial-costs-south-carolina: The national cemeteries are in Beaufort, Florence and Columbia, and the state-run M.J. Dolly Cooper cemetery is in Anderson, in the Upstate.
burial-costs-new-hampshire: New Hampshire has no national cemetery; its state veterans cemetery is in Boscawen, north of Concord.
burial-costs-tennessee: Of Tennessee's five national cemeteries, only Chattanooga and Mountain Home still take casket burials.
funeral-costs-mississippi: Mississippi's three national cemeteries, in Biloxi, Corinth and Natchez, all take burials, and the state adds veterans cemeteries in Kilmichael and Newton.
funeral-costs-wisconsin: With Wood National Cemetery in Milwaukee closed to new burials, a Milwaukee-area family often looks at the state cemetery in Union Grove instead.
funeral-costs-indiana: For a casket burial, Marion is the one Indiana national cemetery still open; the other two take cremated remains only.
funeral-costs-indianapolis: The Crown Hill annex is on West 42nd Street in Indianapolis and accepts cremated remains only, so an Indianapolis casket burial in a national cemetery means Marion, about 70 miles to the northeast.
funeral-costs-nevada: Elko National Cemetery is not yet open, so a Nevada veteran's funeral usually ends at the state cemetery in Boulder City or Fernley.
funeral-costs-north-carolina: North Carolina's four state cemeteries are in Black Mountain, Goldsboro, Jacksonville and Spring Lake.
funeral-costs-south-carolina: Fort Jackson National Cemetery is on Percival Road in Columbia.
funeral-costs-connecticut: That state cemetery is in Middletown.
funeral-costs-massachusetts: Massachusetts National Cemetery is in Bourne, on Cape Cod.
funeral-costs-illinois: Abraham Lincoln National Cemetery is in Elwood, southwest of Chicago.
funeral-costs-ohio: Ohio's open national cemeteries are in Dayton and in Seville, Medina County.
funeral-costs-pennsylvania: Washington Crossing National Cemetery is in Newtown, Bucks County.
funeral-costs-michigan: Great Lakes National Cemetery is in Holly, northwest of Detroit.
funeral-costs-oregon: Willamette National Cemetery is in Portland.
cremation-costs-south-carolina: The Florence site that takes new interments is the national cemetery annex on Stockade Drive.
cremation-costs-south-dakota: Black Hills National Cemetery is near Sturgis.
cremation-costs-vermont: The Vermont Veterans Memorial Cemetery is in Randolph Center.
